source.snippet: Ran into this while swapping external drives between Windows and Mac -- it seems the only reliable way to keep the benefits of NTFS (journaling) and allow writes from MacOS is to use third-party $ commercial drivers. I am not knowledgeble about what makes a driver so I asked (Gemini) -- and I am told this involves a fairly complex low level OS hooks and bypassing OS protections etc with a lot of edge cases -- so today's frontier models are unlikely to produce a reliable driver implementation

problem_statement: macOS users who regularly swap external drives with Windows machines must pay for third-party commercial NTFS drivers to get write access; no free or built-in solution is reliable, creating a recurring paid-software purchase for a basic interoperability need.
target_segment: Mac users who share NTFS-formatted external drives with Windows machines — prosumers, freelancers, small studios, IT staff at mixed-OS offices.
notes: Poster explicitly notes the only reliable path requires spending money on commercial drivers (e.g., Paragon, Tuxera). Paying buyer signal is clear: this is already a paid category with established competitors. Opportunity is either a cheaper/simpler alternative or a SaaS sync bridge. Weak signal volume (single post, 3 pts) but confirms an existing paid market.
